claims.text: A Keycloak realm holds one system's users and signing keys and can hold several RSA signing keys at once; Keycloak signs new tokens with the active key of the highest priority, and the other enabled keys stay published so tokens they signed still verify.
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Administration Guide: Configuring realm keys > Rotating keys; Managing keys (active/passive, priority)

claims.text: Keycloak's guide: add new keys with a higher priority; new tokens are then signed with them, and after a while the old keys can be removed. The lesson's condition for 'after a while' is: once every access token the old key signed has expired.
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Administration Guide: Configuring realm keys > Rotating keys

claims.text: A JWT's header carries kid, the id of the key that signed it, which tells the verifier which public key from the key set to use.

With AddJwtBearer, when a token names a kid not in the cached keys, validation fails (401) and, because RefreshOnIssuerKeyNotFound is true by default, a new download of metadata and keys is requested; it runs in the background.

Requested downloads happen at most once per JwtBearerOptions.RefreshInterval, 5 minutes by default, counted from the last requested refresh; a request inside that interval waits until it has passed. No api restart is needed.

The api keeps the keys it downloaded until its next download (after a start, on an unknown kid, or every AutomaticRefreshInterval), so a key removed from Keycloak is still accepted by the api until then.

A PostgreSQL role, here donhang, the account the api logs in as (Username=donhang), has a single password; ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD replaces it. Authentication happens when a connection opens, so connections already open keep working and new ones need the new password.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: ALTER ROLE; Client Authentication (ch. 20); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/rotate-db-password.txt; scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh:29

claims.text: rotate-signing-key.sh lines 50-55 create a new rsa-generated RS256 key, priority +10, named rotated-<epoch>, via kcadm.sh in the keycloak container of the Compose system (docker compose exec); api_status calls the Compose api at localhost:8080.

Lines 58-60 get a new token and confirm its kid is the active key's and differs from the old token's; lines 66-70 retry GET /api/v1/orders every 5 s for up to 360 s until 200; at the end both tokens get 200.

The realm's access token lifespan is 300 seconds (the output's last line reads accessTokenLifespan); a later run's housekeeping (lines 30-39) deletes retired keys once the newest rotated key is older than that lifespan.

rotate-db-password.sh line 30 runs ALTER ROLE donhang PASSWORD in the db Pod; a session opened before (lines 20-23) finishes; a new connection with the old password is refused, with the new one connects.

Line 49 reseals db (POSTGRES_PASSWORD) and api (ConnectionStrings__Default) via seal-secrets.sh --no-commit; line 15 reads the current password from Secret db; line 50 raises donhang/db-password-version in envs/staging/api.yaml; line 52 commits.
In envs/staging/api.yaml the api reads ConnectionStrings__Default from Secret api via env/secretKeyRef, and the Pod template carries the annotation donhang/db-password-version.
Environment variables from a Secret are set when the container starts and are not updated when the Secret changes; the Pod must be restarted or replaced to see the new value.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Concepts > Configuration > Secrets (Using Secrets as environment variables; env not updated after Secret update)

claims.text: A Deployment rollout is triggered when its Pod template changes, including a change to the template's annotations.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Workloads > Deployments ('rollout is triggered if and only if the Deployment's Pod template (.spec.template) is changed')

claims.text: The PostgreSQL image uses POSTGRES_PASSWORD only when it initializes an empty data directory; with an existing database the variable has no effect on the role's password.
claims.source_hint: Docker Official Image 'postgres' docs: Environment Variables (POSTGRES_PASSWORD) and the note that they have no effect with an existing data directory

claims.text: Removing the old signing key and making the api download keys again (for example by restarting it) rejects every access token signed with the old key, even those not yet expired.
claims.source_hint: Follows from claims 3-4: the kid no longer matches any published key; Keycloak Server Administration Guide: Rotating keys

claims.text: Keycloak publishes the realm's public keys at /realms/donhang/protocol/openid-connect/certs (the jwks_uri), reachable from the host at localhost:8180, each with kid and alg; the script gives its new key alg RS256 (line 54).
claims.source_hint: Keycloak docs: OIDC endpoints (certs / jwks_uri); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml:43-47 (web proxies Keycloak on 8180)

claims.text: If the new Pods started before ALTER ROLE, every connection they open would be refused. In this order, only new connections the old Pods open after ALTER ROLE, until the rollout has replaced them, are refused.
claims.source_hint: Follows from claims 7 and 14; rotate-db-password.sh:26-66 (waits for the Argo CD sync and the rollout)
